title: Dad's Call
description:
It was Dad.

A family friend's son is getting married this weekend.
Come home, he said. It'd be nice to go together.

{name} checked the calendar. An investment deadline this week.
Checked the account. Hadn't even had fried chicken this month.

On the other end of the phone, Dad was waiting.

choices.text: Go home. The investment can wait a month.
choices.result_text:
Through the train window, home grew closer.

Dad was there on the platform. His shoulders more rounded than {name} remembered.
At the reception hall, Dad introduced {name} to everyone nearby as 'my son.'

The investment window is gone. But somehow — that night, {name} slept well.

choices.text: Say you'll come next time, for sure.
choices.result_text:
Said you'd come next time, definitely.
Dad said 'okay, I know you're busy.'

Hung up. Opened the calendar. Three days to the investment deadline.

The optimal choice.

title: Friend's Profit Screenshot
description: A friend posted a profit screenshot in the group chat. The thought 'I knew about that one too' loops somewhere in the throat. Hard to tell if it's bragging or bonding, but the envy is real.

choices.text: Congratulate them and quietly mine for info
choices.result_text: Offered congratulations, picked up what I could. Made some money, but felt like I was on the outside looking in.

choices.text: Just say you're jealous — honestly
choices.result_text: Said it straight. The friend actually ended up comforting you. Refreshing and a little bitter at the same time.

choices.text: Jump in and copy the trade immediately
choices.result_text: Followed the friend's move on the spot. People around you are starting to notice you always seem to know something.

choices.text: Steer the conversation somewhere else
choices.result_text: Smoothly changed the subject. Everyone laughed and went home. Easy.

title: Stock Tip DM
description: Another 'insider tips' DM hit the Instagram inbox. Packed with profit screenshots and testimonials. If all of it is real, why would they share it with a stranger?

choices.text: Scam. Block immediately.
choices.result_text: Called it a scam and blocked. Counted the avoided loss as a win — and somehow ₩40,000 came back around.

choices.text: Look for more reviews. Think it over.
choices.result_text: Spent a long time looking into it. Ended up doing nothing. Head full of noise.

choices.text: Put in a small amount to test it.
choices.result_text: Threw in a small stake. Learned something. Also something you'd rather not have in the search history.

title: Can't Sleep Again
description: 2 AM and still awake. Eyes are exhausted but the brain won't stop. {name} knows — the same thoughts, the same hour, the night before too.

choices.text: Set a sleep schedule. Go to bed early.
choices.result_text: Fixed a bedtime, downloaded a sleep tracker. A few days later, the body felt different. A body that sleeps is a body that works — obvious, until it isn't.

choices.text: Too tired to put the phone down, but can't.
choices.result_text: Couldn't put the phone down. Fell asleep sometime in the small hours.

choices.text: Search for sleep aids.
choices.result_text: Looked up sleep aids. Felt a little uneasy leaving that search history behind.

choices.text: Just power through it.
choices.result_text: Decided to push through. Knew the body was taking damage. No bandwidth to change it.

title: Last Winter
description:
December.

The memory of the first night in the goshiwon came back.
The flickering fluorescent light. A thin blanket. The neighboring wall filling the window.

{name} opened the window.
Cold air came in. Seoul was in winter.

Five years had passed.

What was different now?
The room was different. The number in the account. What the years had written on the face.

Some things hadn't changed.
Gangnam was still far. Dad's calls were still short.
Something unnameable remained in the chest.

This is the last month.

choices.text: Focus on what time is left.
choices.result_text:
Closed the window.

No time to think. Or rather — thinking won't change anything.
Do what can be done right now. That's all.

{name} opened the spreadsheet again. You don't know until the end.

choices.text: Slowly look back at every choice made.
choices.result_text:
What if the {name} from five years ago had known all this?

Some of it was right. Some wasn't.
Regrets exist. So does something like — yes, you did what you could.

All of it, together, was {name}.
Somehow that felt okay.

title: The Driver
description:
1 AM. The designated driver arrived.

The moment he got in, he started talking.
'Where are you from? Office worker?'

{name} gave a vague answer. The driver said:
'I used to be a division manager at a mid-size company. Restructuring got me.'

For a second, his eyes were visible in the rearview mirror.
Seoul's night skyline slid across the glass.

'If I'd saved just a little more back then, I wouldn't be doing this.'

Silence. Sleep drained away.

choices.text: Listen without saying much. Nothing to say.
choices.result_text:
At the destination, {name} got out.
'Take care,' the driver said.
'You too,' {name} said.

His name, company, or salary from back then — unknown.
But what he said stayed a long time.

'I used to be.'

choices.text: Ask: how are things now?
choices.result_text:
'Once the kids get through college, things'll pick up,' he said.
'It's fine now. This job isn't bad.'
Whether he meant it — impossible to know.

Getting out, {name} added a little more to the tip.
The driver said thank you.

His voice stayed for a while.

title: Their Passbook
description:
A quick trip home.

Dad was rummaging through a drawer and stepped away.
{name} was tidying absently when a bank passbook appeared.

Knew not to look. Looked anyway.

The balance appeared.

Smaller than expected. Much smaller.
{name} had a rough idea of what Dad earned over the years.
And where it had all gone.

choices.text: Put the passbook back. Pretend nothing happened.
choices.result_text:
Dad came back. Carried on the conversation as if nothing had happened.

Over dinner {name} tried to erase the number from memory.
It wouldn't go.

On the train back to Seoul, a thought settled in.
Maybe everything {name} is doing now exists because of that number.

choices.text: When Dad comes back, say what you saw.
choices.result_text:
'you saw it. You're sorry.'

Dad was quiet for a long time.
'Hey. It's fine.' That was all.

But something shifted after those short words.
Now neither of them had to pretend not to know.

{name} stared out the window the whole ride back.

title: Housewarming Photos
description:
Photos appeared in the group chat.

A college friend. New apartment. Housewarming party. Snapshots.
In the background — the Han River through the window.

Comments started piling up.
'Wow, insane.' 'Honestly jealous.' 'Where is that?'

{name} glanced at the window.
The window looked out at another wall.

choices.text: Send a 'Congrats!' sticker.
choices.result_text:
Sent the sticker.
Put the phone down.
Looked around the room.

Jealous. No more accurate word exists.
Jealous, and happy for them, and someday me too.

That all three of those can be true at the same time felt, somehow, exhausting.

choices.text: Mute notifications. Flip the phone face-down.
choices.result_text:
Another notification arrived. New photos.
Living room. Sofa. Solid wood dining table.

{name} put the phone in a drawer.

Early morning tomorrow. Do what can be done today.

Thought that. Twice.

title: Old Colleague, Gangnam
description:
A familiar face on a Gangnam street.

A former coworker. Left the company around the same time.

But different now. What he was wearing, what he was carrying, even the way he walked.

'Oh — {name}! It's been a while!'

He seemed genuinely glad. {name} was glad too.
Something else was mixed into that gladness.

choices.text: Ask how things have been. Catch up.
choices.result_text:
He'd changed jobs. Got a raise.
Said he lived in an officetel nearby now.

'How about you?' he asked.
'Doing well,' {name} said.

After parting, {name} sat on a bench in the alley for a while.
Couldn't tell if that was a lie or not.

choices.text: Pretend not to see him. Keep walking.
choices.result_text:
Kept walking.

Fifty meters on, wondered if he'd looked back.
Didn't turn around.

That it was the comfortable choice — felt, somehow, melancholy.

title: First Business Card
description:
The first business card with a job title on it.

The team lead handed them over before the first outside meeting.
'You're representing the company now. Do well.'

{name} looked down at the card.

Name. Title. Company. Number.

This small rectangle was {name}'s weight in the world right now.
Five years ago, this was unimaginable.

choices.text: Keep one in the wallet. Go to the meeting.
choices.result_text:
After the meeting, handed one over.
The other person took it naturally, slipped it into their wallet.

A gesture that meant nothing to them.
It meant something to {name}.

On the subway back, opened the wallet and looked at the card again.
A name, pressed into paper.

choices.text: Pause for a moment. It still doesn't feel real.
choices.result_text:
Hand trembled slightly when handing the card over in the meeting.
The other person didn't notice.

Back home, placed a card on the desk.
Looked at it for a long time.

Whether this is the beginning, or the middle of a long road — impossible to say.
But — made it here.

title: The Algorithm Knows
description:
The YouTube recommendations have changed.

Used to be variety shows. Now it's different.
'Essential finances for your 30s' 'How I saved ₩300M through investing' 'The reality of moving to Gangnam.'

Those were the videos {name} had watched.
Those were the words {name} had searched.

The algorithm doesn't lie.
It knew what {name} wanted better than {name} did.

choices.text: Watch one video. Going to sleep anyway.
choices.result_text:
1:47 AM.

Watched one video. The next played automatically.
Related. More related. More related.

Two hours later, {name} had watched a stranger's investing failures from a decade ago.

Whether it was useful — unclear.
Sleep was gone — certain.

choices.text: Close the app. Not sure what I'm doing.
choices.result_text:
Closed the app.
The room went quiet.
Stared at the ceiling.

Do you actually want Gangnam, or am you just anxious?
That line gets blurry sometimes.

Went to sleep. Felt right.

title: A Friend from Home
description:
A message from an old friend.

'Hey, what's it actually like living in Seoul? You think you're fine staying here.'

That friend works at a job back in their hometown.
Doesn't earn much, but has a place to live, family nearby.

'What do you think, {name}? Is Seoul really that great?'

{name} stared at the screen for a moment.

Had no idea what to say.

choices.text: Be honest: 'I genuinely can't say.'
choices.result_text:
'you don't know. Some good things, some hard things.'

Friend replied: 'Still, you've got your reasons for staying.'

That one line was, strangely, a comfort.

There are reasons. Hard to put into words.
That's enough, sometimes.

choices.text: Positive spin: 'Seoul's worth it. So many opportunities.'
choices.result_text:
Friend replied: 'That's impressive, seriously.'

The word 'impressive' felt strange.
Not sure if impressive is the right word.

After hanging up, {name} thought:
Do you stay because Seoul is good — or because leaving feels impossible?

One of those must be true.

title: Night Shift Kindness
description:
2 AM, a convenience store run.

Picked up a triangle kimbap, walked to the register.
The part-timer said while scanning:

'There's one with thirty minutes left on the label — want it? We'd just throw it out.'

{name} looked at them.
Looked like a student. Someone working nights.

The kindness had no special reason. That made it linger.

choices.text: Say thanks. Take it.
choices.result_text:
Walked out with two rolls of kimbap.
Sat on the bench outside and ate.
Tasted fine.

That part-timer is out here holding on too. Or maybe it's just a part-time job.

Either way — their kindness was the warmest thing that night.

choices.text: It's okay. Leave it.
choices.result_text:
Walking out: 'Should have taken it.'

Thought about going back. Kept walking.

Seemed like nothing. Kept coming back to mind.
If you'd taken it, you'd have eaten it and forgotten.

title: Five Years in Seoul
description:
Moving boxes — something fell out of one.

Things brought up from home when first coming to Seoul.
An old pair of earbuds. A blank notebook. A business card from back then.

What did that {name} think this city would be?

Five years have passed.
Better off than then? Honestly — hard to say.
Something has definitely changed.

choices.text: Throw it out. No time to be tied to the past.
choices.result_text:
Closed the box. Put it in recycling.

Those things from before — gone.

Not regretful. A little regretful.
Both of those were true at the same time.

Looking forward doesn't mean erasing the past.
It just means looking forward.

choices.text: Take a look. Then put them back.
choices.result_text:
Put the box in a corner of the new place.

Someday, these things will come out again.
What will this present moment look like from there?

For now, just have to live.
That was the only thought.

title: Payday
description:
The salary came in.

A notification chimed. The number appeared.
Credit card bill, rent, phone, insurance.

Subtract all of that — not much left.

That's what's left to live on this month.
That's the value {name} produced this month.

Stared at the number for a while.

choices.text: Figure out how to save even a little more.
choices.result_text:
Decided to cut back on food. One fewer coffee.

Saved ₩50,000.

₩50,000 seems small.
But that's ₩600,000 in a year.
₩6,000,000 in ten.

The face doing that math — sometimes, felt a little sorry for it.

choices.text: Eat something good today. Invest in yourself.
choices.result_text:
Went out. Ate well.
Good. ₩30,000.
Worth it. A little not worth it.

Both of those coexisted through the whole meal.

Next month will be better.
Decided to believe that.

title: The Neighbor Next Door
description:
You ran into them in the hallway.

Around the same age. A brief nod.
Waiting at the washing machine, the conversation started.

'How long have you been here?'

This is how most friendships begin in a goshiwon.
Tight space, shared circumstances, accidental timing.

choices.text: Strike up a comfortable conversation
choices.result_text:
You learned their name. And that you're in the same boat.
For the first time in Seoul, you had someone you knew.
The goshiwon felt a little less foreign.

choices.text: Give a brief nod and head back to your room
choices.result_text:
They seemed decent, but you were too tired today.
You'd run into them again.

title: The Café Regular
description:
The small café next to the convenience store you visited every day.

Today the staff member spoke to you first.
'You come in every day. Iced Americano, right?'

Someone you didn't even know by name had memorized your order.
In Seoul, something like this turned out to be unexpectedly comforting.

choices.text: Warmly keep the conversation going
choices.result_text:
A conversation that lasted maybe ten minutes.
You shared a little about work, Seoul, and dreams.
You had a feeling you'd be back tomorrow.

choices.text: Just smile and take your coffee
choices.result_text:
Today you just drank the coffee.
That was enough.

title: The First Automatic Rent Transfer
description:
A text arrived about the automatic rent transfer.
{name}'s bank balance was thin from the start, and Seoul didn't wait for anyone.

choices.text: Cut living expenses even further
choices.result_text: You shifted the ratio from convenience store lunches to home-cooked meals. The bank account held on, but your spirit was wearing thin.

choices.text: Look for weekend part-time work
choices.result_text: You hustled through every weekend shift. An extra ₩150,000 came in, but your body was truly hitting its limit.

choices.text: Study investing to find a way out
choices.result_text: Pressured by the rent, you decided to break through by studying investing. Nothing changed right away.

title: A Call from Your Parents
description:
Sunday afternoon, 3 PM. 'Mom' lit up on the screen.

You already knew what was coming as you pressed accept. They'd ask how things were going. You'd say you were fine.

'Are you eating properly?'

On the desk in your room sat a convenience store lunch box. The third one today.

'Yeah, eating well.'

choices.text: Avoid money talk and just exchange pleasantries
choices.result_text: You kept it to small talk. You couldn't bring yourself to say things were hard, but just hearing your mom's voice made things a little better.

choices.text: Open up and admit you're struggling
choices.result_text: When you admitted how hard it was, your parents went quiet. Your chest felt lighter, but you felt guilty for worrying them.

choices.text: Talk big and say you'll be making a lot of money soon
choices.result_text: You talked a big game about getting rich soon. Only after you hung up did you feel a little ashamed of yourself.

title: A Job Posting Appeared
description: A headhunter sent a LinkedIn message. An offer for a position paying 20% more than your current salary. But you'd only just started settling in with your current team.

choices.text: Carefully compare the salary and conditions
choices.result_text: You laid everything out in a spreadsheet. The job search prep cost ₩220,000, but your head felt clearer.

choices.text: Reassure yourself that your current job is better
choices.result_text: You talked yourself into believing the current job was still the better option. The anxiety settled, but an uneasy feeling lingered.

choices.text: Send in your résumé right away
choices.result_text: You submitted your résumé and your team leader found out. The office atmosphere turned strangely awkward.

title: Election Season Thematic Stocks
description: As elections drew near, stock app notifications exploded. Group chats went wild over stocks tied to certain candidates. You started wondering whether this was investing or gambling.

choices.text: Study the risks of thematic stocks first
choices.result_text: You did your homework before diving in. The timing worked and you came out with a profit, and people started talking.

choices.text: Just watch the news and gauge the mood
choices.result_text: You spent the whole day refreshing the news. In the end you did nothing and the stress just piled up.

choices.text: Buy a small position for now
choices.result_text: You bought a small position. Luck was on your side, and people around you started to take notice.

title: Reserve Training Notice
description:
A text arrived with a civil defense training notice.

Received at 9:12 AM. You were in the middle of a meeting.
33 years old. Your reserve years ended two years back, and now it's these texts. You've aged, alright.

You checked the date. A Friday morning that week of all weeks. The day before an important deadline.

Getting this worked up over a half-day lecture — you really don't have much slack these days.

choices.text: Check the date and apply for half-day leave
choices.result_text: You checked the date and took a half-day. Only the morning to clear — better than the old reserve days.

choices.text: Grumble about it with old army buddies
choices.result_text: You vented to your old buddies and the group chat lit up. "Wait, we're on civil defense now?" — everyone suddenly felt old.

choices.text: Search whether online training qualifies
choices.result_text: You looked into the online-training criteria. If it qualifies, finish from home; if not, off to the hall. Made a note either way.

title: Broken Phone
description:
You dropped your phone coming down the stairs.

There was a sound. Glass shattering. It bounced once and landed face-down.

You picked it up slowly. The screen was cracked like a spiderweb.

Repair estimate: ₩300,000. New device: ₩1,000,000.
You couldn't bring yourself to open your banking app. You just stood on the stairs for about three seconds.

choices.text: Get a cheap replacement from a secondhand site
choices.result_text: You scoured a used phone site and found a deal. It worked better than expected and oddly cleared your head.

choices.text: Keep using it with the cracked screen and feel miserable
choices.result_text: You kept using it with the cracked screen. Every time you looked at it, your mood sank.

choices.text: Splurge on a brand-new phone on installments
choices.result_text: You bought the latest phone on installments. The reaction from people around you was good, but you worried about your account balance.

title: Housing Lottery Frenzy in the Group Chat
description:
A housing subscription notice went up in the group chat.

Total points tallied, estimated competition ratios, odds simulators.
Comments flooded in. 'Should I open a subscription account now?' 'How does the no-home period calculation work?'

{name} didn't even have a subscription account. That fact suddenly stung today.

It felt like everyone else knew the rules of a game you hadn't even heard of.

choices.text: Calmly verify the subscription conditions
choices.result_text: You went through the subscription criteria step by step. It cost ₩450,000, but you confirmed you met the conditions.

choices.text: Get even more confused by the flood of information
choices.result_text: There was too much information and it only made things more confusing. You didn't know what to believe and went blank.

choices.text: Just apply without thinking it through
choices.result_text: You just hit apply. Your attitude was: if it happens, it happens.

title: Family Medical Bills
description:
Your parents called. The hospital bill came out higher than expected.

You heard the amount. You ran the numbers. You quickly calculated the maximum you could pull from your account right now against the remaining expenses for the month.

It felt strange to be running these calculations. When did your parents' hospital bills become a 'line item'?

There was no way to calculate the weight of that guilt.

choices.text: Decide on an amount you can realistically send
choices.result_text: You sent only what you could manage. Your parents said they were fine, but your heart felt heavy.

choices.text: Stew in guilt and lose sleep over it
choices.result_text: You stayed up all night with guilt. You did nothing while slowly eating yourself alive.

choices.text: Take out a loan and cover the full amount
choices.result_text: You took out a loan and covered everything. Your family was grateful, but the next few months were going to be tight.

title: Leaving Early, Are We
description:
The evening team meeting ended.

Everyone returned to their seats when the team leader called {name} over.
'You seem to be leaving early lately.'

A quiet voice. Two colleagues behind you stopped in their tracks.
Three seconds to respond.

choices.text: Say you'll wrap up your tasks first
choices.result_text:
You reached for a notepad. Bent your head like you were writing something.
The team leader walked away. So did the colleagues.
The office went quiet as if nothing had happened.

choices.text: Feel wronged, but nod anyway
choices.result_text:
'Yes, understood.'
It took two seconds to get those three words out.
On the subway home, those words kept echoing. Leaving early, are we.

choices.text: Say 'I always leave after finishing my work'
choices.result_text:
The team leader paused for a moment.
'Alright.' That was all.
You felt the other colleagues watching. You weren't sure if that was the right call.

title: Health Checkup Results
description: The health checkup results came in. Words like 'borderline value' and 'follow-up monitoring required' caught your eye. Whether this was a real problem or not, you couldn't judge on your own.

choices.text: Book a consultation with a doctor
choices.result_text: You booked a doctor's consultation. It cost ₩50,000, but it was better than vague anxiety. Knowing is better than not knowing.

choices.text: Put the results sheet in a drawer and forget about it
choices.result_text: You put the results in a drawer and forgot about it. Playing ignorant was more comfortable for now.

choices.text: Look up the condition yourself online
choices.result_text: You searched for the diagnosis online. It only made you more frightened, and you trembled through the night.

title: Jeonse Scam in the News
description:
News headline: 'Villa King victims number 127, combined deposits total ₩2.8 billion.'

You stopped mid-read.

A name surfaced in your memory. The name on the stamp at signing.
You suddenly weren't sure whether that was the same name on your current jeonse contract.

Five minutes passed in a state of rational-yet-irrational fear.

choices.text: Check the property registry right now
choices.result_text:
You opened Government24.
You found the landlord's name. There was a mortgage lien.
The figure was bigger than you expected. Bigger than your deposit.

choices.text: Tell yourself it can't be your place and turn off the news
choices.result_text:
You turned off the TV.
Two days later, a similar story ran again.
{name} turned off the news that time too.

choices.text: Call the landlord immediately
choices.result_text:
It rang. No answer.
You sent a text. No reply.
You held your phone in your hand all night.

choices.text: Turn off the news and don't think about it
choices.result_text:
Next month's maintenance bill arrived.
Same address. Same landlord's name.
Nothing happened. This time.

title: AI Face-Reading App
description:
An AI face-reading app was trending on social media. Upload a photo of your face and it tells you your fortune and career aptitude.

You found it absurd, yet there you were downloading the app anyway.

You took a photo. Analyzing. Three seconds.

Result: 'Wealth luck: low. Interpersonal relations: medium-high. Caution during job changes.'

You started to delete it, then read it one more time.

choices.text: Laugh it off and move on
choices.result_text:
You looked at it and laughed. The results were so outrageous it was even funnier.

As you deleted the app, you thought: people don't look at this stuff just for fun.

choices.text: Stare at the results and genuinely reflect
choices.result_text: You studied the results seriously. It was ridiculous, but oddly it stayed with you.

choices.text: Eagerly share it with everyone around you
choices.result_text: You shared it and everyone tried it. You became the center of attention, but felt a bit embarrassed about it later.

title: A Sibling's Request
description: A KakaoTalk message from your sibling. 'Hey, could I borrow ₩500,000 for a bit...' You're barely scraping by yourself, but you can't bring yourself to say no to family. You can't tell whether this person is just the kindest soul or the biggest pushover.

choices.text: Set a clear limit on what you can give
choices.result_text: You drew a clear line on what you could manage. You lent ₩100,000 and said the rest wasn't possible. Your sibling said they understood.

choices.text: Cave and lend the full amount
choices.result_text: You caved and lent everything. Your account was emptied and you had no idea if you'd ever see it back.

choices.text: Say you'll lend it with interest — and make them promise
choices.result_text: You said you'd lend it with interest and made them promise. Your sibling sulked for a moment but said thanks later.

choices.text: Pretend you didn't see it and delay replying
choices.result_text: You kept putting off the reply. Your body felt fine, but a corner of your mind wouldn't let it go.

title: Resignation Vlogs
description:
1:30 AM.

YouTube recommended a video: 'Quit My Job and Lived in Jeju for a Month.'
You clicked. Autoplay kicked in. You clicked again.

Third video. Outside the window it was still dark.
The person in the video looked free by any measure.

{name} already knew. That reality wasn't like that.

choices.text: Calculate whether you have six months of living expenses
choices.result_text:
You opened a calculator.
The number came out. Not enough.
You played the video again. This time you watched to the end.

choices.text: Subscribe to the channel and close the tab
choices.result_text:
You hit subscribe.
You closed the tab.
In the morning you got up and got ready for work. Same as always.

choices.text: Draft a resignation letter in Notepad
choices.result_text:
You wrote the first line.
'I wish to resign effective the end of this month.'
You read it three times. You closed it without saving.

title: The Secondhand Haggler
description:
You listed something on Daangn and a comment appeared.

'Could you do ₩30,000? I'll come pick it up right away.'

You'd listed it at ₩50,000. Why does this person always offer 60% of the asking price? Is this an unspoken rule? Some law of the Korean secondhand market?

₩30,000. ₩50,000. There was ₩20,000 between them.

choices.text: Sell at the offered price
choices.result_text: You sold at the offered price. ₩30,000 came in and the transaction was clean.

choices.text: Get tired of haggling and just sell

A screenshot showed up on the Instagram feed.

'2024 returns: +31% proof~'

147 likes.

Or maybe there was no account yet.

This feeling that everyone was making money — what was it?

choices.result_text:
VOO, SPY, TIGER US S&P500.
You saved a comparison chart of expense ratios.
It wasn't copying — it was research. Probably.

choices.result_text:
You tapped the heart.
Scrolled to the next post.
That one post lingered in your mind for two days.

choices.text: Open a brokerage account right now
choices.result_text:
You downloaded a brokerage app.
Account setup took 12 minutes.
The hand reaching for the first buy button trembled slightly.

title: A Rainy Night at Gangnam Station

choices.text: Get soaked and let the mood wash over you
choices.result_text: You let yourself get soaked and leaned into the feeling. The mood was strange, but your body felt clammy.

choices.text: Ask a passerby if you can borrow their umbrella
choices.result_text: You asked a stranger to borrow their umbrella. The other person looked uncomfortable and you felt a bit embarrassed.

title: Lunar New Year Family Gathering
description:
The first question came the moment you sat down.

'Have you found a job? What about marriage?'

It was your aunt. You hadn't even eaten yet.
Beside you, your cousin quietly bowed their head.
For a moment, only the sound of the children in the room seemed loud.

choices.text: Make up being busy and change the subject
choices.result_text:
'Things have been a bit hectic with a project lately.'
Your aunt nodded.
The next question went to your cousin beside you. Five seconds of reprieve.

choices.text: Grit your teeth and eat the meal
choices.result_text:
You ladled the soup.
You didn't answer.
The food didn't go down easily.

choices.text: Say your goodbyes and leave early
choices.result_text:
'I actually have something going on today.'
You felt your mother watching.
You sighed on the bus. But it was a relief.

title: A KakaoTalk at 8:02 PM
description:
On the subway.
8:02 PM.

A KakaoTalk from the team leader arrived.
'Can you do overtime tonight?'

You had plans. Or maybe you didn't.
There was time to reply. Three minutes until the next station.

choices.text: Honestly reply that you have plans tonight
choices.result_text:
'I actually have prior plans tonight.'
You sent the reply and put the phone in your pocket.
No reply came from the team leader. That bothered you more.

choices.text: Feel guilty and agree to the overtime
choices.result_text:
'Yes, I'll be there.'
You sent a cancellation text for your plans.
Overtime ended at 11 PM.

choices.text: Reply that you've already left for the day
choices.result_text:
'Ah, I just stepped out.'
It was a lie. You were still on the subway.
A reply came. 'I see. Good work today.'

choices.text: Read it and don't reply
choices.result_text:
The read receipt appeared.
You flipped the phone face-down.
The next morning was going to be uncomfortable.

title: The Bill After Drinks

choices.text: Feel annoyed but pick up the whole tab
choices.result_text: You were annoyed but you covered it. The mood lifted, but your wallet felt lonely.

choices.text: Say you're covering tonight so they'll get next time

title: Real Estate Regulation Rumor

choices.result_text: You waited for the official announcement. ₩170,000 came in, but the wait wore on your nerves.

choices.text: Anxiously keep refreshing the real estate forums all day
choices.result_text: You refreshed the real estate forum all day. In the end you accomplished nothing and were completely drained.

choices.text: Trust the rumor and search for distressed listings
choices.result_text: You trusted the rumor and searched for distressed properties. People around you acknowledged the move, but you had no idea if the call was right.

title: One Big Score and It's All Over

choices.text: Coolly look up the statistics
choices.result_text: You coolly looked up the stats first. Seeing the expected value always in the negative as a hard number, the impulse faded.

choices.text: That line keeps going around in your head
choices.result_text: The line kept circling in your mind. You couldn't shake it for a good while.

choices.text: Place a small bet just to see
choices.result_text: You placed a small bet. The outcome was bad and you learned that line was a lie.

title: The Finance YouTuber's Dance
description:
A YouTube thumbnail appeared: 'How I Bought a Gangnam Apartment in My 30s.'

2.8 million views. 12,000 comments saying 'Thank you for sharing.'

You clicked. A 6-minute 12-second video. The first 4 minutes 30 seconds were his success story. After that — insurance pitch.

{name} closed the tab. But the words 'Gangnam apartment in your 30s' stayed lodged in your head.
That was the video's real purpose.

choices.text: Turn it off and study with a book instead
choices.result_text: You turned it off and opened a book. ₩130,000 came in and your focus was sharper.

choices.text: Watch it to the end with a laugh
choices.result_text: You laughed your way to the end. The stress relief was real, but an hour had already passed.

choices.text: Subscribe and buy the paid course
choices.result_text: You subscribed and bought the course. You maybe learned something, but telling people about it later felt a bit embarrassing.

title: A Partner's Real Question
description: Six months in. Your partner asked: 'Where do you see us going?' Emotionally it was great, but realistically you felt uneasy. Speaking your truth might mean someone getting hurt.

choices.text: Be honest about your realistic plan
choices.result_text: You laid out a realistic plan honestly. Your partner nodded and grew serious.

choices.text: Say love is enough, that's all that matters
choices.result_text: You said love was enough. You got through the moment, but something told you the same question would come again.

choices.text: Promise things will be better than they are now
choices.result_text: You promised things would get better. Your partner smiled, and it became a promise you'd made to yourself too.

title: Promotion Evaluation Season
description: HR announced the quarterly review results. Your name was on the candidate list. Word came through that your supervisor had been keeping an eye on you. How you played this opportunity was going to matter.

choices.text: Work overtime without complaint and deliver results
choices.result_text: You pushed through two straight months of overtime and finally got the promotion. Your salary rose and your business card changed, but your body was reaching its limit.

choices.text: Keep performing steadily and wait for the outcome
choices.result_text: The result was pushed to next quarter. But your supervisor started remembering you as 'the consistent one.'

choices.text: Go directly to your supervisor and show your drive
choices.result_text: You went directly to your supervisor and showed your motivation. No promotion this round, but the next opportunity was clearly closer.

title: Conflict with a Colleague
description: A colleague on your team presented your idea as their own. The team leader already praised them for it, and you're the only one who knows the truth.

choices.text: Quietly let the team leader know the truth
choices.result_text: You quietly brought it up with the team leader. They read the situation and started giving you more speaking time in meetings. Things got awkward with the colleague, but your standing improved.

choices.text: Hold it in for now and wait for the next opportunity
choices.result_text: You swallowed it and moved on. Your chest burned, but you avoided a direct confrontation. You promised yourself next time your name would go first.

choices.text: Confront the colleague directly
choices.result_text: You confronted them directly. The colleague was thrown off, but the tension spread through the whole team. Your chest felt lighter, but the aftertaste was bitter.

title: Through the Goshiwon Walls
description:
1 AM. Sobbing from the next room.
The walls are so thin you can hear even breathing.
{name} was like that at first too.

choices.text: Knock on the wall and ask if they're okay
choices.result_text: You knocked to ask if they were okay, and a moment later came a short 'Yes, thank you.' You didn't know each other's names, but something felt connected.

choices.text: Put in earphones and pretend not to notice
choices.result_text: You put in earphones and lay down. The sound was gone, but that person kept coming to mind.

choices.text: Leave a drink from the convenience store at their door
choices.result_text: The next morning there was a thank-you note stuck to the door. No name, but it was there.

title: Shared Bathroom Rush Hour
description: 8 AM. Four people in line for the shared bathroom. You have an interview at 9, and a shower is out of the question.

choices.text: Use just the sink quickly and head out
choices.result_text: You couldn't wash your hair, but you made it out somehow. You could only hope the interviewer wouldn't notice.

choices.text: Go to a nearby jjimjilbang to wash up
choices.result_text: ₩12,000 felt steep, but stepping out freshly clean, your confidence was on a different level.

choices.text: Wait in line
choices.result_text: You waited 20 minutes and barely made it. You weren't late for the interview, but your heart was racing the whole time.

title: A Room With No Window
description: You didn't see sunlight today either. There are no windows in the goshiwon. You check your phone to find out if it's morning or evening.

choices.text: Go to the Han River for some fresh air
choices.result_text: You sat on a bench along the Han River for thirty minutes. Watching the sun go down, you thought: tomorrow will be a little better.

choices.text: Decide to get used to the dark
choices.result_text: You thought you were fine, but after days without going outside, your body felt damp and heavy.

choices.text: Buy a small plant to keep in the room
choices.result_text: You bought a succulent from the plant stand in front of the convenience store. Small and tough — it reminded you of something.

title: Dreaming of Moving Out
description: You opened a real estate app. A studio in Gwanak-gu for ₩400,000. When your pay goes up, next month, always 'when.' It keeps going.

choices.text: Open a dedicated savings account for moving costs
choices.result_text: You put ₩30,000 into a 'moving fund' account. A start is half the battle, you told yourself.

choices.text: Accept that it's not realistic right now and let it go
choices.result_text: You closed the app. Not yet. But when would 'yet' ever arrive?

choices.text: Look into share houses
choices.result_text: You spent a while reading share house reviews. There's the roommate risk, but it might still beat living alone.

title: Line 9 Rush Hour Hell
description: Line 9 on the morning commute. You can barely breathe. Someone's bag is digging into your back, sweat and body odors mingling. And this repeats every single day.

choices.text: Get off one stop early and walk
choices.result_text: Ten extra minutes of walking, but the air was different. Those ten minutes might be what gets you through the day.

choices.text: Put in earphones and endure it
choices.result_text: You maxed out the volume. Your body was in hell, but at least your mind was somewhere else.

choices.text: Grab a taxi
choices.result_text: You muttered 'just this once' and got in. Watching the subway hell recede behind you — half guilt, half relief.

title: Convenience Store Lunch Again
description: A ₩4,900 lunch box. One minute thirty seconds in the microwave. This was dinner. You checked the expiration date one more time.

choices.text: Just make do with this
choices.result_text: It didn't taste great, but your stomach was full. Getting used to this taste was the scarier part.

choices.text: Go home and at least boil some ramyeon
choices.result_text: You cooked ramyeon with YouTube playing in the background. Thirty minutes that felt less alone.

choices.text: Treat yourself to a proper meal today
choices.result_text: A bowl at a rice soup place. The broth was hot and salty. But why did you almost tear up?

title: The Han River Chimaek Temptation
description: Your friends want to go for chicken and beer at the Han River. This month's living budget is tight — but then again, so is life.

choices.text: Go — you only live once
choices.result_text: The night view was beautiful. Any thought about the money disappeared after the first piece of chicken.

choices.text: Lie about being sick and skip it
choices.result_text: Staying home alone, FOMO hit hard. You blocked the Instagram stories. But at least you saved the chicken money.

choices.text: Buy convenience store beer and join them
choices.result_text: It was just convenience store beer, but being together made it good. Nobody cared what you were drinking.

title: Opening the Delivery App
description: Exhausted after work, you opened a delivery app. Minimum order: ₩18,000. To eat alone you'd spend over ₩20,000. Plus a ₩3,000 delivery fee.

choices.result_text: You waited 30 minutes and ate. It was good. You decided not to look at the card statement.

choices.result_text: You didn't want to go out, but you did. The wind was cold. That wasn't so bad either.

title: The Night Before the Interview

title: One Finance Self-Help Book

choices.result_text: You worked up the courage to decide. For today, that was enough.

title: Tears Came for No Reason

{name} came home, closed the door, and immediately started crying.
Nothing particularly bad had happened.
You must have just been worn out.

choices.result_text: You tried to erase the feeling. But feelings don't disappear just because you ignore them.

title: Negative Balance

title: Rainy Season Commute

'Thank you for your application. After reviewing your documents,

A cup of coffee.
Rejection is part of the process.

Qualifications, cover letter, work history...

An empty alley.

The officer said, 'People like you still exist, huh.'

A flicker of guilt came and went.

The lien amounts listed on the title register were unsettling.

'Do you know if there's noise coming from above?'
