choices.result_text: The upstairs neighbor was apologetic. It got noticeably quieter after that. You're glad you spoke up.

choices.text: File a complaint with the building management
choices.result_text: It got handled, but things got awkward whenever you passed each other in the hallway.

choices.text: Buy earplugs and just endure it
choices.result_text: Fell asleep with earplugs in. This is what surviving in Seoul looks like.

title: Zero-Spend Month Challenge
description:
A 'zero-spend month challenge' is trending on social media.

No coffee, no eating out, nothing but essentials.
Test how much you can save by minimizing all consumption.

{name} looked at the bank balance this month.
Worth trying.

choices.text: Go all in. No eating out for a full month.
choices.result_text: Thirty days. No restaurants. The savings were real. The willpower cost was also real.

choices.text: Set a moderate goal — cut spending by 50%.
choices.result_text: Cut half the usual spending. Not perfect, but sustainable. Small discipline stacks up.

choices.text: Give up — restricting this much is too stressful.
choices.result_text: Decided not to. Frugality that kills morale isn't real frugality. Another way will present itself.

title: Leaked Salary Table
description:
One accidentally shared file spread through the entire team.
A salary table, broken down by rank.

A colleague one year younger than {name} was earning 20% more.
Same hours, same work, different number.

Should you be angry? Did you negotiate badly? Or did they just do it right?

choices.text: Request a salary renegotiation with HR
choices.result_text: They agreed faster than expected. Nothing changes if you don't ask.

choices.text: Start preparing to switch jobs
choices.result_text: Updated the résumé. Confirmed that this company isn't the whole world.

choices.text: Pretend you never saw it
choices.result_text: Even playing dumb, your body knew. Performance dropped noticeably the following month.

title: Wrong Chat Room
description:
You sent a message in a rush.

Only after sending did you realize.
It went to the all-company announcement channel instead of the team chat.

'What's everyone getting for lunch today?' was just sent to all 200 employees.
Read receipts were climbing past 120.

choices.text: Quickly post 'So sorry about that!'
choices.result_text: Someone replied to the apology: 'I was wondering too.' You were able to laugh about it two days later.

choices.text: Roll with it — respond confidently with 'How about samgyeopsal?'
choices.result_text: The manager said, 'Oh, that's slick.' You turned a crisis into a moment. Seoul respects that.

choices.text: Stay silent and wait it out
choices.result_text: Someone was still chuckling in the hallway the next day. In Seoul, this kind of humiliation becomes small talk material.

title: Payday Emptiness
description:
The 25th. Paycheck arrived.

The balance ticked up with an alert.

But rent, insurance premiums, phone bill, and credit card payments had already been deducted.
The money spent less than 48 hours in the account.

'Is this how I survive a whole month?' The thought crossed your mind.

choices.text: Go through every expense one by one
choices.result_text: Cancelled two unnecessary subscription services. Small savings become habits.

choices.text: Accept it — this is just reality
choices.result_text: Payday emptiness might just be the rite of passage into adulthood.

choices.text: Resolve to increase income through a side gig or investments
choices.result_text: A resolution alone creates direction. Next month might look a little different.

title: A Stranger in a Café
description:
A café in front of a real estate agency.

The man in his fifties at the next table hung up his call and muttered to himself.
'Still don't know that market.'

Your eyes met. He smiled and asked.
'Where do you live? How much are you paying for rent these days?'

He said his name was Im Sangchul. The name meant nothing, but his eyes were interesting.

choices.text: Tell him your situation honestly.
choices.result_text:
Sangchul nodded and handed over his card.
'You look like someone trying to become something. Let's grab coffee sometime.'

choices.text: Give a vague answer and leave.
choices.result_text: Something unusual about that man. You found out later — he was well known in Gangnam real estate circles.

title: Sangchul's Call
description:
You thought it was an unknown number. It was Im Sangchul.

'I was passing by and thought of you. Doing alright?'

No real reason for the call. Just checking in.
Before hanging up, he added one thing.

'The mood in that neighborhood lately feels off. Just keep it in mind.'

choices.text: Ask him for more details about that neighborhood
choices.result_text:
Sangchul smiled and shared a few more things.
'I like that you're here to learn. That's the most important thing.'

choices.text: Just say thanks and hang up
choices.result_text:
Someone in this city was thinking of you.
That alone made the day feel strangely solid.

title: A Bowl of Gukbap
description:
Sangchul said he'd buy lunch.

Not somewhere expensive. A gukbap place in the market alley.

'I've eaten lunch here for thirty years. What I've made in real estate has nothing to do with where I eat lunch.'

He poured kimchi broth into his gukbap and said,
'The more you deal with money, the more you can't let money own you.'

choices.text: Sit with those words
choices.result_text:
That bowl of gukbap stuck with you longer than any lecture.
Chase money, but don't let money chase you.

choices.text: Smile and say, 'I still need to get to Gangnam though.'
choices.result_text:
Sangchul let out a hearty laugh.
'Right, that's the spirit. Just don't forget what I said.'

title: Time Left
description:
He looked at the calendar.

Less than a year left until he turns 38.

He thought back to himself when he first came up to Seoul, five years ago.
The now he'd imagined back then, versus the now that's actually here.

What will he do with the time left?
Actually — what will he not do?

choices.text: Go all out until the end. No regrets.
choices.result_text:
Last year. He's come this far, so he's going to see it through.
His heart beat fast. Not a bad feeling.

choices.text: Focus on protecting what you've built
choices.result_text:
Not losing is also a strategy.
He decided to spend the final year reinforcing what he'd built.

choices.text: You're starting to think Gangnam isn't everything
choices.result_text:
There are things you only see after running five years.
Where the finish line is — maybe that was his to decide.

title: Last ₩1,000
description:
Your account balance is at the bottom again.
By the convenience store register, one lotto ticket for ₩1,000.

Exactly ₩1,000 left in change.

{name} thought for a moment. Odds of 1 in 8,145,060.
You don't need to do the math. It's an impossible number.

And yet, strangely, your hand reached for it.

choices.text: Buy it — just this once. (−₩1,000)
choices.result_text:
Quick pick. Just wait until Saturday.
The cheapest dream in life.

choices.text: Don't buy it — the odds are absurd
choices.result_text:
You put the ₩1,000 back in your pocket.
A grown-up decision. Not a painless one either.
Just... that.

title: Saturday Night, 9 PM
description:
Saturday night, 9 PM. You opened the lotto app.
Checked the numbers.

...3 matches. 5th prize. ₩5,000.

At first you laughed. Then it was just absurd.
Then funny again.

₩5,000. A ₩1,000 investment, 5x return.
ROI of 400%.

{name} couldn't tell anyone that night.
Too ridiculous.

choices.text: Get some chicken tomorrow. (+₩4,000 net profit)
choices.result_text:
₩4,000 net profit. Tax-free.
The most modest victory in this city.
That chicken tasted unusually good.

title: 15 Months in Seoul
description:
Fifteen months since you came to Seoul.

Today a hometown friend posted on social media.
'Finally got the apartment lottery! Moving in two years' — 147 likes.

{name} closed the screen. Opened it again. Closed it again.

The distance left to Gangnam was a number you knew.
Today, for the first time, that number felt real.

choices.text: Leave a congratulations comment. Genuinely.
choices.result_text:
You left a congrats comment. It was genuine. Half of it.

You looked up what floor plan they were getting. Not sure what you were hoping to find.
You closed the window and opened your budget spreadsheet. Start with what you can do now.

choices.text: Close the app. You move at your own pace.
choices.result_text:
You closed the app.

Someone else's pace can't become yours. {name} knew that.
Still, you stared at the ceiling a long time that night.

choices.text: Start researching the apartment lottery system.
choices.result_text:
You printed the lottery eligibility scoring sheet. Years without owning property, dependents, savings account payments.
Numbers filled every line.
Late to the game, but knowing beats not knowing.

title: Halfway
description:
Thirty months.

Half of five years has passed.

You held a cup of coffee and looked out the window. You thought of the goshiwon where you unpacked your bags the day you first arrived in Seoul. What was your goal back then?

You calculated the gap between your current balance and your target.

Halfway there. Or not even halfway.
The remaining thirty months felt shorter than the first thirty.

choices.text: Look back on the choices you've made so far.
choices.result_text:
The good calls. The bad ones.
The regrettable choices. The fortunate ones.

Add them all up and you're here. Save the regrets for tomorrow — today, think about the thirty months left.

choices.text: Change strategy. The current approach isn't working.
choices.result_text:
You pulled out a calculator. Current asset growth rate, time remaining, required return.

Numbers don't lie. Something had to change.
What exactly — still unknown.

choices.text: Check whether speed matters less than direction.
choices.result_text:
Gangnam is still the goal. That much is right.
But today was the first time you seriously asked why it had to be Gangnam.

No answer yet. But having the question itself was something.

title: 15 Months Left
description:
Fifteen months left until the date you marked on the calendar.

It started as sixty months. Now it's fifteen.

Not sure if having less time left is a relief or pressure.
They say the closer the deadline, the sharper your focus.

{name} looked out the window. Seoul was busy as ever today.
What about you?

choices.text: Make a plan for the final sprint.
choices.result_text:
You opened a notebook. Listed everything still doable in fifteen months.

The list was longer than expected. This many things still undone.

Starting now.

choices.text: Think about what meaning these five years hold, apart from the outcome.
choices.result_text:
Whether you make it to Gangnam or not.

Over these five years, {name} earned money for the first time, lived alone for the first time, experienced real failure for the first time.

You think you'll understand what that means later.

title: Father Was Hospitalized
description:
A call from your mother.

Your father had collapsed, she said. Nothing too serious, but could you come visit?

{name} looked at the calendar. This month was also packed.
Looked at the account. Still far from the goal.

Mother was waiting.

choices.text: Go down. This time, you go.
choices.result_text:
The hospital corridor was quiet.

Your father was asleep. He looked smaller than you remembered.
Your mother said 'You came.' Two words. That was enough.

On the KTX back to Seoul, for the first time in a long time, your mind went blank.

choices.text: Say you can't make it this time either.
choices.result_text:
Mother said 'That's alright, if you're busy.'

You hung up and looked at the monitor. The charts were there. The numbers were there.

Was this the optimal choice this time too?

title: School Reunion
description:
The high school group chat buzzed.

Let's get together. This Saturday in Hongdae.

When you got there, everyone had changed a lot.
Some had jobs, some were married, some had started businesses.

'What are you up to these days?' someone asked.
Everyone was listening.

choices.text: Be honest. Say you're working toward a goal.
choices.result_text:
A brief awkward silence.

Then one person said 'That's impressive — I don't even have goals like that.' Everyone chimed in. Better than expected.

You told your story. That was it.

choices.text: Say things are going well. Skip the details.
choices.result_text:
Everyone nodded.

Someone posted the group photo on Instagram on the way home.
Caption: 'Good to see everyone doing well.'

{name} hit like.

choices.text: Change the subject. Ask about the others.
choices.result_text:
Everyone got busy talking about themselves.

{name}'s update never came up.
On the bus home you stared out the window.

Next time, you want to have something worth saying.

title: That Thing You Said
description:
A text from one of the reunion crowd.

'Hey, you said things were going well back then. Teach me some investing too.'

{name} stared at the screen for a moment, then closed the message.
The reunion came to mind.

choices.text: Come clean. Tell them you're still in the middle of it.
choices.result_text:
The friend went quiet for a moment.
Then said, 'I get it. Honestly things aren't going that great for me either.'

You texted for another hour. First real conversation in a while.

choices.text: Brush it off vaguely.
choices.result_text:
You were vague. They probably saw through it.

After that, it got harder to reach out to them first.
Lies accrue interest in relationships.

title: Are You Happy?
description:
One night, for no particular reason.

The question came.

Are you happy?

choices.text: Yes.
choices.result_text:
Yes.

Gangnam is still far. The account is still short.
But — yes.

You hoped that answer was genuine.
It probably was.

choices.text: I don't know.
choices.result_text:
You don't know.

You're not sure what happiness is. No reference point.
Will you know once you've hit your goal? Or will you still not know then?

Not knowing was the most honest answer tonight.

choices.text: No.
choices.result_text:
No.

Saying it honestly was strangely freeing.

Not happy. Not yet.
So then — when can you be?

Having that question felt like the beginning of something.

title: Promoted
description:
You made assistant manager.

A cake appeared, applause followed, the team leader reached out to shake hands.
{name} smiled. This was the moment to be happy.

Later, alone in the bathroom.
You looked in the mirror.

Assistant Manager {name}.
Was this what you wanted?

choices.text: You're pleased. Next target: manager.
choices.result_text:
You ate the cake. It was good.
Jotted down the next goal. Manager.
The face in the mirror was just the face in the mirror.

choices.text: Pause — is this really what you wanted?
choices.result_text:
You finished the cake.
The question didn't go away.

I don't know. Right now, you're just — an assistant manager.

title: Late Night at the Office
description:
11 PM. Still in the office.

Your phone buzzed. A former colleague who went into investments.
'Crypto +38%. Got out of work early today, saw the chart and got in. Sweet dreams.'

{name} looked at the monitor.
Half the report was still left.

choices.text: Finish the report. This is your path.
choices.result_text:
You finished the report.
It was 1 AM.
You didn't reply to your colleague.

choices.text: Reply: 'Nice. I'm still doing overtime.'
choices.result_text:
You sent the reply.
They said 'Hang in there.'

You looked at the monitor again. Half the report still left.

choices.text: Call it a night. Finish the report in the morning.
choices.result_text:
You shut the computer off.
Made a plan to come in early.
The night air was cold outside.

title: Employee of the Month
description:
You received the outstanding employee award.

Your name was engraved on a plaque. The CEO shook your hand.
A photo was taken. Applause rang out.

On the bus home, you took the plaque out of your bag.

{name}'s name.

You felt nothing.

choices.text: Put the plaque on your desk. You're proud.
choices.result_text:
You put the plaque on the corner of your desk.
Colleagues said 'Impressive.'
{name} smiled.

choices.text: Come home and put the plaque in a drawer.
choices.result_text:
Into the drawer.

A plaque with your name on it.
Not sure if this was the way you imagined making your name — not sure at all.

title: A Senior's Farewell
description:
A senior colleague who'd worked there for thirty years retired.

At the farewell dinner, the senior said,
'I just... kept showing up, and thirty years went by.'

Applause came. A cake came.
{name} clapped and thought:

'Just kept showing up, and thirty years went by.'
Would you end up saying the same thing?

choices.text: Lasting thirty years like that is also something to admire.
choices.result_text:
You told the senior 'I respect that.'
They smiled.
'I just kept going.'

{name} knew: enduring is also a skill.

choices.text: Decide you want a different kind of life.
choices.result_text:
Walking home, you typed in your phone notes:
'What will I say in thirty years?'

No answer. But having the question might be the start of something.

choices.text: Pour another drink. Tonight, you just drink.
choices.result_text:
You refilled the soju glass.
Sat next to the senior and just drank.
Decided not to think tonight.

title: Father's Voice
description:
Sunday evening. A call from your father.

'Are you eating properly?'

That was always the whole of it. But this time there was a longer silence after.

Something he wanted to say but didn't. His voice was slightly different.

choices.text: 'Dad, how are you feeling? Are you seeing a doctor?'
choices.result_text:
There was a brief pause.
'...Nothing major. Just taking blood pressure medication.'

You sat still after hanging up.
Your father always said 'nothing major' his whole life.

choices.text: 'Yes, eating fine.' Just exchange greetings.
choices.result_text:
Ten minutes of chatting, then hung up.

Later, word came from an aunt. Your father had been seeing a doctor lately.
You could have heard it straight from him.

title: Going Home
description:
You went home for the first time in a long while.

Father's house was unchanged. The floral calendar over the refrigerator, the photo frames beside the TV.

Your father had cooked. Doenjang jjigae and grilled mackerel.

'Is it good?' he asked.
'Yes.' You meant it.

choices.text: Spend a long time talking. Even bring up the scam.
choices.result_text:
Your father waved his hand at first.
Then slowly said, 'I was greedy. That's on me.'

Those words stayed with you.
Your father never blamed others. Not once in his life.

choices.text: Eat and head back quickly. Work has piled up.
choices.result_text:
On the KTX racing back to Seoul, you thought:

Next time, you'd stay longer.
But you didn't know when that next time would be.

title: Father's Words
description:
After finishing the doenjang jjigae, your father brought it up for the first time.

'I was being greedy. Wanting a Gangnam apartment — that was my greed.'

A long silence.

'But you... you're doing well. Better than I did.'

choices.text: 'You did well, Dad. It wasn't greed.' You say it.
choices.result_text:
Your father looked out the window.

After a long pause he said, '...Thank you for saying that.'

That was all. Your father was never a man of many words.
But that was enough.

choices.text: Say nothing. Just sit beside him.
choices.result_text:
Your father said nothing either.

The two of you sat there for a while.
You could see the neighborhood outside the window. The one your father lived in his whole life.

Even if you make it to Gangnam someday, you think you'll remember the smell of this house.

title: The Bus Home
description:
You walked out of the Jeongseon casino.

You got on the bus.
Mountains blur past the window.

You calculate in your head what you lost today.
You keep recounting the same number.

Doesn't matter how many times. It's always the same number.

choices.text: It was entertainment money. Just call it fun.
choices.result_text:
You settled on that conclusion.

You half believed it.
Not completely.

{name} didn't take out the phone all the way to the terminal.

choices.text: Never going back. For real this time.
choices.result_text:
Hard to say how long that resolve will last.

But in this moment, it was sincere.

The bus pulled away. {name} closed his eyes.
Sleep wouldn't come all the way over the mountains.

title: One More Round
description:
The money you won today is in your wallet.

You're on the way home but your feet won't move.

You were lucky today.
And when you're lucky, the luck keeps going. — At least right now, {name}'s brain is saying exactly that.

choices.text: Go back in. Today's your day.
choices.result_text:
You went back in.

The second session was different.

You left with barely anything in your pocket.
The casino always works this way. It never sends you home at your best moment.

choices.text: Quit while you're ahead. Go home.
choices.result_text:
You turned around.

Not an easy decision.

{name} today — at least on this one call — made the right move.
The walk home felt lighter.

title: Why Am I Here Again?
description:
Walking out of the Jeongseon casino, a thought struck you.

It was just going to be once.

At some point, you'd started calculating Jeongseon casino dates in your head.
You'd memorized the bus schedule.

{name} paused for a moment.

choices.text: Put some distance between you and it. No visits for a month.
choices.result_text:
You made the decision.

Nothing grand. Just one month.

One month was enough to create distance.
How hard that would be — you still didn't know.

choices.text: It's still under control. I can stop whenever I want.
choices.result_text:
That's what you said.

To yourself.

One of the most common symptoms of addiction is the conviction that you're fine — {name} doesn't know that yet.

title: Rent Day
description:
The calendar app showed 'Rent' again.

₩520,000 for the goshiwon. At least electricity and water are included, small comfort.
You opened the account. The balance stared back.

You know you have to pay. But what's left after is the problem.

What if the landlady quietly knocks — you were holding your breath inside the room.

choices.text: Transfer immediately (₩520,000)
choices.result_text:
Transfer complete. The balance dropped visibly.
Relief that you survived another month, and dread at having to do it again — both arrived at once.
The room was quiet.

choices.text: Hold on this month — ask the landlady to wait a few days
choices.result_text:
The landlady said 'Well, what can you do,' but her expression said otherwise.
You started avoiding her eyes whenever you crossed paths in the hallway.
The thing poor people lose most is their dignity.

title: Two Triangle Kimbap
description:
Today's meal was handled at the convenience store.

Two triangle kimbap, ₩2,400 total.
You ate standing by the refrigerator — not because there was nowhere to sit, but because sitting felt more pathetic somehow.

The part-time worker at the register seemed younger than {name}.
The thought flashed through your mind: that kid is earning a paycheck right now.

choices.text: Another day survived. That's enough.
choices.result_text:
Walking back to the goshiwon under the streetlights.
Half-full stomach, half-empty heart.
Maybe a job call comes tomorrow.

choices.text: Go into the nearby gukbap place — spend ₩5,000 and eat properly
choices.result_text:
One spoonful of hot broth and you almost cried.
You felt human again after eating.
You didn't know ₩5,000 could mean this much.

title: Job Board All-Nighter
description:
11 PM. Alternating between Jobkorea and Saramin, hitting refresh.

'3+ years experience preferred' — where's a fresh grad supposed to get 3 years?
'Age no barrier' — then why is there a birth year field?
'Self-starter required' — what does that even mean?

Opened 27 listings. Closed them.
Applied to 2.

Only the monitor's glow filled the room.

choices.text: Spray and pray — apply to everything in sight
choices.result_text:
Applied to 15 listings. Copy-paste cover letters, just changed the company name.
Not a bad strategy. It's a numbers game.
Results usually come back about two weeks later.

choices.text: Focus on one and polish the cover letter
choices.result_text:
You worked on one cover letter until 2 AM.
The quality went up. Your eyes felt like they were falling out.
You hit submit and lay down.

title: Friend's First Day at Work
description:
Scrolling, a photo from a college classmate appeared.

'First day as a new employee! Starting with excitement :)'

In the photo, they were in a dress shirt, photographed in front of a station.
Comments read 'You worked hard,' 'Finally!' 'Buy me dinner lol' in a row.

{name} didn't leave a comment. Didn't even hit like.
Just turned the phone face down.

choices.text: Leave a congratulations comment — no comparisons
choices.result_text:
'Congrats! You'll do great.' You left it.
It wasn't 0% genuine.
But posting it made you feel emptier.

choices.text: Delete the social media app — block the comparison
choices.result_text:
You pressed the delete confirmation.
Quiet settled in.
Not looking at other people's success isn't defeat.
{name} right now needed focus, not comparison.

title: Blind Date
description:
A friend set up a blind date. Age, job, looks — from what you've heard, not bad.

Being set up at 33 feels a bit awkward, but there's a saying that awkward is opportunity.

What will you do?

choices.text: Go. Curious to see what kind of person they are.
choices.result_text: You spent two hours at a café. No strong spark, but you laughed listening to someone else's life for the first time in ages. Meeting people can be this light.

choices.text: Don't go. You don't have the bandwidth for this right now.
choices.result_text: You declined. Your friend was disappointed. Whether this was the right call — unclear. Something else comes first right now.

choices.text: Go, but without any expectations.
choices.result_text: Went without expectations, came back without expectations. But the walk home didn't feel like walking alone. Strangely, the mood was good.

title: Coworker Tension
description:
A coworker on your team keeps catching your eye. Over lunches together, over late nights.

You know that something with a coworker gets complicated. Even so — you can't stop noticing.

choices.text: Try expressing your feelings.
choices.result_text: You said it. They looked startled. Things got awkward. But — it beat thinking about it constantly. Clarity beats awkwardness.

choices.text: Just stay friends. Work is work.
choices.result_text: You acted normal. They did too. Things will probably flow naturally from here. This feels right for now.

choices.text: Create some distance. Can't let work get complicated.
choices.result_text: You pulled back a little. They seemed to notice. Work efficiency held. You choose to believe this was the right call.

title: Ex's Message
description:
A message from a former partner you haven't heard from in a long time.

'Doing okay?' Three words.

You've read those three words about ten times, trying to figure out what's behind them.

choices.text: Suggest meeting up.
choices.result_text: You sat in a café for about an hour. Talked about old times a little. Coming out felt like something had been resolved. Not bad.

choices.text: Reply briefly that you're well, then nothing more.
choices.result_text: 'Yeah, doing fine.' You sent it. No more conversation. That was enough. It's already over.

choices.text: Read it and leave it.
choices.result_text: You read it. Didn't reply. Didn't sleep well. Still okay. It ended for a reason.

title: Dating App
description:
A friend convinced you to download a matching app.

A few photos and one line about your job. Picking people from this feels strange, but apparently everyone meets this way now.

Want to make a profile?

choices.text: Write it seriously. Exactly as you are.
choices.result_text: You wrote it honestly. '33, currently navigating a life pivot.' Matches were sparse, but strangely, writing a self-introduction made you rethink who you are.

choices.text: Polish it a bit. Everyone does that, they say.
choices.result_text: Made it sound good. Got a match. Already tired before meeting them. Do I have to keep up this version of myself?

choices.text: Download it, then delete it ten minutes later.
choices.result_text: Doesn't seem like the right moment. Deleted. Something else is more important right now.

title: English Lessons
description:
A senior at work said it: 'Your pay is different if your English is good.' Right now you can't even write a basic email in English.

There's a conversation school nearby. ₩250,000 a month.

choices.text: Enroll. It's an investment.
choices.result_text: You went to the first class. The levels varied wildly. You weren't the worst. You think you can keep going.

choices.text: Learn from YouTube for free.
choices.result_text: Found a YouTube channel. Fifteen minutes a day. Slower than a school, but free. Right for your situation now.

choices.text: Not now. Once you're settled.
choices.result_text: Decided later. When exactly 'later' is — unclear. Something else comes first now.

title: Coding Course
description:
A coupon arrived from an online learning site. Python intro, originally ₩49,900 on sale for ₩1,900.

You read somewhere that knowing how to code these days can generate side income. Not sure if it's true.

choices.text: Buy it. ₩1,900 investment.
choices.result_text: Paid. Got through 3 sessions. It's interesting. Not sure if you'll finish it — but you started.

choices.text: Buy it and set a goal to complete it all.
choices.result_text: Paid and blocked it in the calendar. 'Complete in one week.' Goals change how you act. Got through 5 sessions.

choices.text: You'll probably never finish it anyway. Don't buy.
choices.result_text: Didn't buy. There are already a few courses you've never finished. That's the reality.

title: Investment Seminar
description:
Sangchul sent a link. Free personal finance seminar. 'If you already have investment instincts you don't need it, but might be worth going once.'

Saturday afternoon, two hours. In Yeouido.

choices.text: Go. There might be something you don't know.
choices.result_text: You went. 70% was stuff you already knew. Something in the other 30% was worth keeping. One sentence from the presenter stuck with you. That's enough.

choices.text: Self-study is more efficient.
choices.result_text: You spent that time reading instead. Things you already knew. Still, re-reading shows you new things.

choices.text: Follow Sangchul there. The connections matter too.
choices.result_text: Sangchul knew a lot of people there. The dinner after the seminar was more valuable than the seminar itself. People are information.

title: Language App — 30 Days
description:
There's a language learning app on your phone. You installed it a month ago, did it for three days, and stopped.

A notification came today. 'Come back. Earn a badge for 30 consecutive days.'

You don't need the badge — but you've never once hit 30 days in a row, and that bothers you.

choices.text: Set a goal of 30 consecutive days. Start small.
choices.result_text: You did 30 days. Your language skills didn't leap forward. But the feeling of doing something every single day — that was different. Next month's goal formed itself.

choices.text: Delete the app. Pointless notifications.
choices.result_text: Deleted. You didn't like being pulled in by badge rewards. If you really need it, you'll re-download.

choices.text: Just do it today. Tomorrow is unknown.
choices.result_text: Did 10 minutes today. Tomorrow is unknown. Still, that's better than yesterday.

title: Sleep Debt
description:
Was up all night doing something. Couldn't sleep.

Woke up with a heavy head.
This has been going on for three days now.

choices.result_text:
Seven hours. First time in a while.
Next day my head felt different. So this was the normal state.
choices.text: Tonight I sleep early, no excuses

choices.result_text:
Two coffees. Pushed through. The work got done.
But the body remembered.
choices.text: Push through on coffee — I have things to do

title: To Work Out or Not
description:
Made it all the way to the gym door.

Go in or not. You were tired.
But you've lost count of how many times you've used that excuse to skip.

choices.result_text:
Thirty minutes. The first ten were the hardest.
On the way out you thought — yeah, glad you came.
choices.text: Go in

choices.result_text:
Came home. Lay down.
Figured you'd go next time. Always did.
choices.text: Rest today

title: Skipped a Meal Again
description:
Too busy to eat.

Or more precisely, chose not to. Couldn't be bothered.
You were hungry. But going out to get something felt like too much.

Third time this month already.

choices.result_text:
A convenience-store rice ball and milk. 8,000 won.
Felt human again after eating.
choices.text: Go out and eat something

choices.result_text:
Decided to eat in the morning instead.
Maybe your body felt a little lighter, maybe not.
choices.text: Just sleep

title: Lower Back
description:
Your lower back hurt.

Thought it was odd at first, but now it's stiff every morning.
The goshiwon mattress? Your posture? Your age?

You're thirty-three.

choices.result_text:
Orthopedics. X-ray. 50,000 won.
Muscle tension, they said. Stretch more, they said.
50,000-won advice, but it put your mind at ease.
choices.text: Go to the hospital

choices.result_text:
Endured it. Too busy.
By next month it had gotten worse.
choices.text: Just endure it — too busy

choices.result_text:
Looked up back stretches on YouTube.
Ten minutes. Felt a little better.
choices.text: At least stretch

title: A Cold
description:
A tickle in your throat, then a runny nose.

A cold.

Bad timing to get sick. It always was.

choices.result_text:
Cold medicine. Rested a day.
Next day you were 70% recovered. Glad you caught it early.
choices.text: Buy medicine and rest up

choices.result_text:
Pushed through. It took a week.
More things fell apart in the meantime.
choices.text: Push through and keep going

title: Checkup Notice
description:
A text about the national health checkup arrived.

You were eligible this year. Free.

{name} saw the text and swiped it away. Too much hassle.
But you couldn't remember the last time you got checked.

choices.result_text:
Booked the hospital. Blood test. Chest X-ray.
When they said 'all clear,' the relief was bigger than expected.
Thought you wasn't worried about your health — turns out you were.
choices.text: Make an appointment

choices.result_text:
Thought, later.
Later will come. When, you don't know.
choices.text: Later

title: My Eyes Are Killing Me
description:
Stared at your phone too long and your eyes stung.

A screen-time alert popped up. 7 hours 48 minutes today.

How did it come to this. You didn't even really do anything.

choices.result_text:
Turned the phone off at ten and read a book.
The first ten minutes your hand kept reaching for the phone.
Thirty minutes later you were just reading.
choices.text: Turn the phone off early tonight

choices.result_text:
Said you'd do a little more, but nothing useful came of it.
Lay down to sleep and your eyes kept blinking.
choices.text: Do a little more

title: Migraine
description:
One side of your head throbbed.

A stress migraine. Comes once or twice a month.

{name} knew where the painkillers were. Inner pocket of the bag.

choices.result_text:
Lay down for twenty minutes. Felt better when you got up.
It was the body's way of telling you to rest.
choices.text: Take medicine and lie down a bit

choices.result_text: Just endured it. Two hours later it got worse.
choices.text: Just endure it

title: What to Eat
description:
Lunchtime. {name} stepped outside.

Left: gukbap, 7,000 won. Right: convenience-store lunchbox, 4,500 won.
Straight ahead: 24-hour half-and-half chicken, 17,000 won.

Never thought one meal in Seoul could be this complicated.

choices.result_text:
A hot bowl of gukbap.
Warmed me up. Worth the 7,000 won.
choices.text: Gukbap — take care of myself

choices.result_text:
4,500 won. Ate it. Felt empty.
A meal that fills the stomach but not much else.
choices.text: Convenience-store lunchbox — save money

title: A Signal
description:
One of those days you didn't want to do anything.

There were things to do. But your body wouldn't move.
Outside the blanket felt too far.

{name} thought — is this burnout?

choices.result_text:
Spent the whole day under the blanket.
Guilt at first, then after a while it was okay.
Tomorrow felt like it'd be different.
choices.text: Take the day off — for real

choices.result_text:
Forced yourself up. Did something.
The body moved but the head was gone.
Efficiency was under half.
choices.text: Force myself up

title: 20 Minutes to Decide Lunch
description:
"What should we eat today?"

It's been twenty minutes since that question.

Chicken? Had it yesterday. Gukbap? Sick of it. Pasta? Someone said it's pricey.
Chinese? The dip-or-pour tangsuyu debate alone would eat ten minutes.

{name} was hungry. Lunch break was shrinking.

choices.result_text:
"I'm going to the convenience store."
Done in five minutes. Back before the meeting.
Leadership, in the end, is making a decision.
choices.text: Just pick somewhere and be done

choices.result_text:
Ended up at the gukbap place and was five minutes late.
The team lead saw. Said nothing, because he was late too.
choices.text: Keep debating

title: Elevator to the 2nd Floor
description:
Got on the elevator alone.

Pressed the button for the 2nd floor.

The moment the doors closed, you realized the stairs would've been faster.
Too late.

{name} faced forward. Waited for the number to change from 1 to 2.

choices.result_text:
2nd floor. Doors opened.
No one there. A relief.
choices.text: Just ride it — already on

choices.result_text:
Made a vow.
Took the elevator again the next day.
choices.text: Use the stairs next time (a vow)

title: War With the Printer
description:
The printer wouldn't work.

Power on. Connected. But not working.

Off and on. Reinstalled the driver. Connected by USB. Reconnected by Wi-Fi.
Thirty minutes passed.

The assistant manager next to me came over. Pressed one button. It worked.

choices.result_text:
The assistant manager grinned and left.
{name} made a note of that button.
choices.text: Thank you (sincerely)

choices.result_text:
"Just because." The assistant manager left.
{name} pondered ten more minutes. Still no idea.
choices.text: How does it work (sincerely)

title: The 1+1 Trap
description:
Went to the convenience store.

Went in for one rice ball,
Then found a buy-one-get-one sale.

Snacks. Drinks. Ice cream. Cup ramen.

At the register you were holding five things.
Originally 3,500 won, but it rang up 11,000.

choices.result_text:
Have to buy it. 1+1 must be bought.
Got home, opened the fridge. Already had two of the same thing.
choices.text: Buy it all — 1+1 cannot be refused

choices.result_text:
Paid just the 3,500 won.
Kept thinking about the 1+1 on the way out.
Not sure if you did the right thing.
choices.text: Buy only what I came for

title: The Empty Seat
description:
There was an empty seat on the subway.

{name} and the person beside you spotted it at the same time.

A half-second exchange of glances.

choices.result_text:
Sat down. The other person sat right next to you.
Both pulled out our phones. Seoul.
choices.text: Sit down

choices.result_text:
Gestured. The other person sat, gave a nod.
{name} grabbed a strap and stood.
Not a bad feeling.
choices.text: Give it up

title: The Group Chat
description:
200 messages had piled up in the company group chat.

Checked at lunch — they were all reactions to one notice the team lead posted at 9 AM.

"Thank you" "Noted" "Understood"

198 of them.

{name} wondered if he had to send one too.

choices.result_text:
Sent it. The 199th 'Noted.'
The team lead replied with an emoji.
choices.text: Send 'Noted'

choices.result_text:
Didn't send it. There's already 200.
No one noticed. Probably.
choices.text: Don't send — it's already 200

title: Café Seat Wars
description:
Walked into a café.

No seats. Of the 15 tables, 12 had no people — just belongings.

The belongings were waiting for their owners.
Probably.

choices.result_text:
Waited 30 minutes by a table with stuff on it. The owner came back. Said they'd gone to the bathroom.
A 30-minute bathroom break.
choices.text: Wait beside a table with belongings

choices.result_text:
Went to another café. Same situation there.
But you snagged a window seat. Felt like a win.
choices.text: Go to another café

title: Got Off at the Wrong Stop
description:
Dozed off on the subway and got off at the wrong stop.

When you opened your eyes, the doors were closing.

The station name was different. Two stops past yours.

choices.result_text:
Waited six minutes for the next train, smiling. No big deal.
Some days are like this.
choices.text: Smile and wait for the next train

choices.result_text:
Got angry at yourself. Figured you'd lost six minutes.
Later, you never once thought about those six minutes again.
choices.text: Get angry at myself

title: Betrayed by Autocorrect
description:
Sent a text, then looked again.

"Are you free for a meeting tomorrow"
went out as "Are you free for a meating tomorrow."

The other person had already read it.

choices.result_text:
"*meeting, sorry T_T"
The other person replied 'lol.'
Might have come across as human.
choices.text: Send a correction right away

choices.result_text:
Said nothing.
The other person said nothing either.
The meeting got scheduled.
choices.text: Let it go — context makes it clear

title: Enter the Golden Boy
description:
Mom called.

"You know Minsu next door? He got into a big company. Getting married too, I hear."

{name} remembered Minsu. Dead last in class senior year.

"That's great, good for him."

Mom paused for a moment.

choices.result_text:
"I'm doing fine too."
"Right, of course you are."
Mom hung up.
{name} wondered if something was, in fact, going fine.
choices.text: "I'm doing fine too"

choices.result_text:
"...Yeah." (Silence)
Hung up.
Wondered again if Minsu really was last in class. Seemed right.
But it didn't matter now.
choices.text: "...Yeah" (silence)
